newsitem.title: UK: Coffee lower, subdued and watching New York.
newsitem.headline: Coffee lower, subdued and watching New York.

text.p: Coffee came lower in more subdued trade on Wednesday morning, traders said.
It had been called around $50 lower on numbers. "I don't think anybody expected it down that much," one trader said.
By the midday break, benchmark July last traded $38 lower at $2,037 per tonne on volume of 631 of a total 1,376 lots.
Further losses were seen as possible in New York adding that "people are talking about lower prices again".
He noted that Monday's gains on London had been given back.

He did not expect a big impact from the Association of Coffee Producing Countries meeting in London. "In theory nothing price sensitive should come out," he said. "People think that most producers have oversold quota anyway."
"The fundamentally bullish picture hasn't changed, but it's all in the market now," he said. More recent news had been neutral or even bearish, but recent selling had been mainly profit taking.
"I don't think that anyone wants to be short in this market," he said, particularly as the frost season was coming up.
